description:
The server, web UI and MCP bridge run on the core's own repository construction, search, document reads and schema instead of private copies. Each change event then costs one repository read on the server, whatever the number of open browser tabs.

## Background

**Construction and watching.** `jit-server` discovers its own layout (`crates/server/src/main.rs:68-75`: `WorktreePaths::detect()` plus `discover_repository_layout`) and builds `JsonFileStorage` from the raw `--data-dir` (`crates/server/src/lib.rs`, `prepare_server_storage`). The CLI uses `WorktreePaths::detect_for_data_root` and `configure_worktree_paths` (`crates/jit/src/main.rs:2466-2491`), which the server never calls. `configure_repository_layout` returns silently when the storage root differs from the layout's data root (`crates/jit/src/storage/json.rs:1050`), so a mismatch surfaces as a 500 on every request rather than at startup. The watcher receives the raw data directory (`main.rs:91`). Its `is_graph_relevant` (`crates/server/src/watcher.rs:77-117`) repeats the core storage names `issues`, `index.json`, `gate-runs` and `gates.toml` as literals. It filters `claims.jsonl` and `claims/`, which live under `.git/jit` outside the watched tree. It ignores `config.toml`, although that file changes `/graph` hierarchy resolution, and the web UI fetches `/config/hierarchy` only on mount.

**Refresh cost.** `web/src/App.tsx:89-92` refetches `/api/issues` on every SSE version bump, and `GraphView.tsx:582` reloads `/api/graph` on the same bump. Both handlers perform a full issue read through `executor.list_issues` (`crates/server/src/routes.rs:82,163`). No response is cached per `ChangeTracker` version, so $N$ tabs cost $2N$ full reads per change. The audit measured `/api/issues` at 3,393,794 B and `/api/graph` at 702,018 B over 1,170 issues. On 2026-10-20 the issue files that `/api/issues` serves whole total 3,714,853 B across 1,186 files. The issue list feeds only client-side search, the label set and dependency titles, and `/graph` already carries id, title, labels and state. No handler uses `spawn_blocking` or `block_in_place`, so file I/O, git and ripgrep processes run on tokio worker threads.

**Search.** Issue search exists three times. `/api/search` runs `jit::search::search` (ripgrep) twice (`routes.rs:309,322`), and the second pass greps `issues/*.json` as text, matching JSON keys and escaped content. `jit issue search` uses the domain `search_issues`. The web scores all descriptions client-side (`web/src/utils/clientSearch.ts`, through `useSearch.ts`).

**Document reads.** `jit doc show` (`crates/jit/src/commands/document.rs:383`) reads an unpinned document from git HEAD through git2, while the server's `read_document_content` (`:567`) reads the working tree. For an uncommitted edit the CLI and the web UI return different bytes. History (`:450`, `:656`) and diff (`:484`, `:700`) also exist as CLI and server copies. `#[allow(dead_code)]` on the public functions at `:566,612,655,699,766` is stale, because `routes.rs` calls them.

**Server surface.** `/status`, `/config/strategic-types`, `/changes` and `/gates/:key` have no production consumer, and neither do the web client methods `getStatus`, `getGateDefinition` and `getDocumentDiff`. The server `StatusResponse` (`routes.rs:220`) copies the core status contract and drops `gated` and `rejected`. `crates/server/src/main.rs:9-12` re-declares the library's `embedded`, `routes`, `sse` and `watcher` modules, so they compile, and their tests run, twice. `git2` and `tower` are declared in `crates/server/Cargo.toml` but unused. Three raw-document handlers repeat one 25-line response block. `infer_content_type` is a hand-written MIME table next to `mime_guess`, and the crate holds two hand-rolled percent codecs.

**MCP bridge.** `mcp-server/lib/cli-executor.js:50-56` unwraps a `success`/`data` envelope that the CLI no longer emits. The instructions (`mcp-server/index.js:41`) list states without `gated` and `archived`. `LONG_TIMEOUT_GATE_VERBS` (`cli-executor.js:153`) is a hand-kept command fact. `_commandPath` and `_hidden` leak into `tools/list`, and each call re-resolves its tool by a linear search. `ConcurrencyLimiter.run` (`mcp-server/lib/concurrency.js:27-46`) decrements `running` and wakes the next waiter on a later tick. A caller arriving in between is also admitted, so more than `maxConcurrent` operations can run.

**Web dead code and layout cost.** `web/src/types/hierarchy.ts` (133 lines) is imported by no file. `subgraphClustering.ts:66` picks the container level with the literal `2` ("typically epic"). Graph layout and refresh search arrays per node: `GraphView.tsx:833` (every SSE reload), `:246`, `:162-166`, and `clusterAwareLayout.ts:90-103`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `jit-server` obtains its storage, repository layout and worktree paths from the same core constructor the CLI uses. The server crate makes no call of its own to layout or worktree discovery.
- [hard] REQ-02: Binding storage to a layout whose data root differs from the storage root fails with an error at construction, and the server exits at startup with that error.
- [hard] REQ-03: The watcher's refresh predicate is one storage-owned allowlist built from the core storage path constants. The server crate contains no storage file-name literals.
- [hard] REQ-04: A change to `config.toml` emits a change event, and the web UI reloads the hierarchy configuration on that event.
- [hard] REQ-05: The web UI makes no `/issues` request in response to a change event. Labels and dependency titles come from the graph response.
- [hard] REQ-06: The server computes the issue list and the graph response at most once per tracker version, however many clients request them.
- [hard] REQ-07: Every handler that reaches the executor goes through one helper. The helper runs the call off the async worker threads and maps its error to an HTTP status.
- [hard] REQ-08: Exactly one issue-search implementation exists. The CLI, the server and the web UI get issue matches from the core domain search, ripgrep runs only over linked documents, and the web client-side scorer is removed.
- [hard] REQ-09: Document content, history and diff are one core method set that the CLI and the server both call. For the same document, `jit doc show` and the server return identical bytes, including an uncommitted working-tree edit to an unpinned document.
- [hard] REQ-10: Every server route and every web client method has a production caller. The server defines no response type that copies a core output type.
- [hard] REQ-11: The server binary uses the library's modules, so each server module compiles once and its tests run once. The server manifest declares no unused dependency.
- [hard] REQ-12: One shared response builder serves raw documents. MIME types come from `mime_guess`, and the server has one percent-coding implementation.
- [hard] REQ-13: The MCP bridge derives its state list, long-running command set and tool metadata from the CLI schema. It keeps no success-envelope handling and dispatches each call by one map lookup. Advertised tools carry no internal fields.
- [hard] REQ-14: The MCP concurrency limiter never runs more than its configured number of operations at once, and a test that admits a new caller during a release proves it.
- [hard] REQ-15: Graph layout and refresh resolve nodes and clusters through indexes built once per pass. No per-node array search remains in `GraphView.tsx` or `clusterAwareLayout.ts`.

## Notes

- Serves @/charter/D-18 (unify and delete parallel mechanism), @/charter/D-20 (one computation per capability: one search, one document read path) and @/charter/D-17 (refresh cost independent of client count).
- Document history and diff reach git through the storage-owned git module required by @/charter/D-21.
- Invariants: @/inv/convention-convergence, @/inv/architecture-dependency-direction, @/inv/single-source-prose, @/inv/canonical-cutover, @/inv/domain-agnostic, @/inv/bounded-rust-build-footprint.
- Ownership (steward, 2026-10-21): epic df129d9e produces the CLI repository bootstrap (storage, layout and worktree construction) and the executor search entry point. REQ-01 and REQ-08 consume those rather than building parallel ones.
- REQ-13 includes `hidden_commands()`: the MCP tool-exclusion policy is derived from `mcp-server/curated-tools.json` or the schema, so no hand-kept duplicate remains.
title: Run the server, web UI and MCP bridge on the core's shared mechanisms
